hypothesis: The AIC8800 runtime reproduces the vendor challenge-reply verifier and the receive/binding behavior over the real controller, card, codec, transport and firmware handoff.

conditions.compiler: Clang 21.1.8, warnings as errors, freestanding AArch64

conclusion: The model passed on the host; no firmware execution, board operation or performance measurement.
narrative: checks/aic8800-runtime.py (removed from the repository; composition covered by aic8800-dispatch and aic8800-data) pinned the published verifier, sender, message definitions, startup caller and receive implementation, compiled the unmodified verifier outside Git with a host identity stub and compared eight challenge/reply vectors against an independent Python SHA-256 calculation; the native worker matched the same vectors. The integrated register model used the real controller, card, codec, transport, firmware handoff and runtime implementations under address/undefined-behavior sanitizers, starting from a simulated completed-start boundary that assumes the preceding firmware execution. Paths passed: binding after a later receive aggregate and an imported early challenge; raw data framing, print/TX-confirmation retention, stale pre-request confirmations, duplicate binding indications and consumer backpressure; platform callback failure and overrun, invalid challenge, malformed challenge or status lengths, truncated data and nonzero binding status; missing confirmation, partial transmission, retained state after fault, idle lease renewal, refusal to revive expiry and first-challenge retention. An initial fixture compile used an incorrect request member name and executed no native model; the corrected fixture allowed the single integrated run to pass, and the already-passing source/vector comparison was reused. A focused follow-up (invalid-platform directory) passed invalid platform callback returns -1 and 2, which must fail under the exact-success contract, while results 0 and 1 stayed as tested. The runtime, transport and changed firmware worker compiled once for freestanding AArch64 (aarch64/results.json records commands, source/object hashes and symbols; dependencies beyond native radio/card/controller APIs are memcpy and memset). final-inputs.json at the evidence root records final source identities, archived inputs and the evidence-reuse rationale. Unchanged SDIO, bootstrap and firmware upload suites were not rerun. Protocol references: kernel revision 2ac08e8c7cdc28abbdc5c9a9dd812f887ae9c79f.
